title: My Chemical Romance Top the Charts, 20 Years On
summary:
Twenty years after its release, My Chemical Romance's "The Black Parade" has reached the top of the Billboard 200 chart. The 20th anniversary deluxe reissue took the top slot, giving the rock band its first Number One album in nearly 25 years together.

The reissue sold 78,000 equivalent album units across more than 20 formats and variants combined, Billboard reports. Released in 2006, "The Black Parade" was the band's third album, a full rock opera in the style of Queen that produced the Top Ten hit "Welcome to the Black Parade." It debuted at Number Two on the albums chart in 2006 and has since become a landmark rock record of the 21st century.

The band celebrated the album's 20th anniversary with a full reissue on October 23, and physical sales pushed it to the top. On Friday, the band also scored its first Number One on the United Kingdom's official album chart.

Notably, the 20-year-old album beat out Olivia Rodrigo's "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So In Love." After midweek predictions showed My Chemical Romance winning by a thousand sales, Rodrigo cheered the band on, posting a clip from their show at New York's Citi Field, which she attended earlier this year. At that show, she met the band and took photos with them backstage.

The chart win comes in the middle of the band's Long Live the Black Parade tour, which kicked off in 2025. Last year they performed at their hometown stadium in New Jersey and took the show to London's Wembley Stadium for two sold-out nights, making the tour a career-defining run.
why_it_matters: Old songs can find new fans decades later, and a comeback like this shows how music can last far beyond its first release.
